value.body: An operations executive keeps a company's daily processes on track, from orders and inventory to vendors and delivery schedules. E-commerce, logistics, manufacturing, retail and service companies hire them. A day involves tracking orders, solving delays, updating reports and coordinating between teams.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA, B.Com or BA; MBA for higher entry

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, ERP systems, ticketing or order-management tools

items.label: Logistics sector employment
items.note: One of several sectors that hire operations staff

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as operations executives or trainees through campus placement, internships or walk-ins. Comfort with Excel and clear communication count heavily in selection.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Excel for reports and data checks

value.title: At a glance
items: Roles vary widely by industry; some are desk-based, others on warehouse or store floors.
Common next roles: operations manager, supply-chain or process-excellence roles.
Shift or weekend work is common in logistics and e-commerce operations.
